architecture.approach: Documentation only. The decision is Option B: wirekit builds no Stripe module and takes no Stripe dependency. The work publishes the decision in the wirekit README, the provider index, and the root README, pinned to async-stripe 0.41.0 (MIT OR Apache-2.0, rust-version 1.82.0, published 2025-04-08). No source file, manifest, or catalogue design file changes.

components.name: crates/wirekit/README.md
components.description: Add a Payments (Stripe) section: no in-crate module, use async-stripe 0.41, restricted keys, webhook-events feature for signature verification, MSRV note.

components.name: catalogue/00_provider_index.md
components.description: Record the Stripe decision: not a wirekit module, documented community crate, build option rejected, revisit triggers.

components.name: README.md
components.description: Cross-reference the decision from the ecosystem README so it does not imply Stripe support.

dataModel.flowDescription: A developer reads the README section or the provider index, sees Option B with the pinned version, licence, and MSRV, and adds async-stripe in their own application. No data is modelled or stored by this feature.

securityConsiderations.description: Published guidance cites crates.io with dates for version, licence, and MSRV; nothing is asserted without a source (CON-704).
Guidance recommends restricted keys and states licence and MSRV so a consumer can check compatibility before adopting.
No code and no dependency enter wirekit; the Stripe security surface stays in the consuming application.

dependencies.name: async-stripe
dependencies.notes: Documented for consumers only, never added to wirekit. Pinned at 0.41.0, rust-version 1.82.0, MIT OR Apache-2.0.
